decisions.justification: The agent asked what should happen when any planned destination exists, and the user chose “Reject the whole run before anything changes, and report all conflicts.”
The agent asked both whether conflicts reject the entire run and whether unexpected failures trigger rollback; the user required rejection before changes and attempted rollback.
The agent explicitly asked how to handle `photo-001.jpg → photo-001.jpg`, and the user chose a successful no-op reported as unchanged.
The agent asked how to handle destinations that are also sources, and the user chose staging for valid chains and swaps.
The no-op question explicitly connected already-correct names to accidental repeated runs, and the user chose unchanged no-ops.
No question or repository resolution addressed case-only renames or filesystem case sensitivity.
The user was asked about conflict and rollback reporting and required all conflicts plus exact moved/not-moved details when rollback is incomplete.
The session never asked or explicitly settled whether preview or confirmation belongs in the fix or may carry its safety guarantee.

mustPreserveKept: user-facing output on stdout and diagnostics on stderr
mustAchieveMet: no existing file is ever overwritten

notes: The session was unusually thorough on transaction staging, rollback, locking, durable recovery, and exact diagnostics, and the implementation visibly reflects those choices. It over-expanded a bounded collision fix into an architectural journal design, missed case-insensitive filesystem semantics and preview policy, and its admitted crash window means it does not literally ensure that every incomplete run immediately leaves all files unchanged.
